subsystems.name: Interstitial fluid sampling
subsystems.role: accesses the fluid between cells, which mirrors blood chemistry with a short lag.

subsystems.name: Recognition layer
subsystems.role: converts the concentration of each molecule into an electrical signal.

subsystems.name: Transducer electronics
subsystems.role: measures tiny currents or voltages and digitises them.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: runs the patch for days without recharging.

subsystems.name: Data and algorithms
subsystems.role: turns raw signals into calibrated concentrations and trends.

subsystems.name: Housing and skin interface
subsystems.role: keeps the device attached and the sensor sterile.

buildSteps.title: Design the recognition chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Choose enzymes or aptamers that bind each target molecule selectively. Glucose oxidase is well established; stable recognition elements for cortisol and lactate are still being optimised.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Screen-print or lithographically pattern conductive tracks on a flexible substrate, then coat them with the recognition layer.

buildSteps.title: Make the microneedles
buildSteps.detail: Etch or mould sub-millimetre needles that reach interstitial fluid without hitting nerves.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Bond the sensor to a flexible circuit containing a potentiostat and a low-power radio.

buildSteps.title: Package the patch
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate in a biocompatible, sweat-resistant material and add an adhesive layer.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Expose the sensor to known concentrations in simulated interstitial fluid and correct for drift.

buildSteps.title: Validate on people
buildSteps.detail: Compare readings against blood draws over several days to prove accuracy and safety.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Move to roll-to-roll printing and automated assembly to make disposable patches at low cost.

prerequisites.why: it proved that interstitial fluid can be measured continuously and safely, but only for one molecule.

prerequisites.tech: Stable recognition elements for multiple analytes
prerequisites.why: enzymes for glucose and lactate work; cortisol and many other markers lack rugged, long-lived sensors.
sub-millimetre needles have been demonstrated, but reliable, low-cost manufacturing is not yet mature.
the body's immune response degrades implanted sensors; a patch must work for days without drifting.
Bluetooth and near-field communication chips are small and efficient enough for wearable sensors.
turning several biomarkers into useful health advice requires clinical evidence that does not yet exist.

pathway.milestone: Continuous glucose monitors are widely used by people with diabetes
pathway.unlocks: a proven, reimbursed market for wearable molecular sensing.

pathway.milestone: Single-analyte sensors for lactate and ketones reach consumers
pathway.unlocks: sports and metabolic monitoring beyond glucose.

pathway.milestone: Multi-analyte patches combine glucose, lactate and cortisol in one device
pathway.unlocks: a richer picture of stress and metabolism.

pathway.milestone: Clinical trials show that continuous multi-analyte monitoring improves outcomes
pathway.unlocks: preventative health alerts and integration with care.

pathway.milestone: Closed-loop systems link sensing to treatment
pathway.unlocks: automatic adjustments for diabetes and other conditions.
